name: broken_rail
revision: r2 (2026-11-10): the r1 critic's and continuity's must-fixes, Pip's recipe for the narrator; see reviews/r1-response.md
caption: why does grandpa wait at an empty rail 🛤️
logline: Every evening for 22 years a villager grandpa has met an empty rail line and said 'She's on her way.' The night his grandson is finally old enough to cross the bridge, he walks the line and finds out why she never arrived.
question: why tf is grandpa waiting for a minecart on a rail nobody uses?
premise: Grandpa (a villager) stands at the buffer stop of the station at the edge of our rail town every evening and has for 22 years. Nothing ever comes down the line. He says 'She's on her way.' Mom says Grandma left him for her sister's village, and kept the cart. Grandpa won't leave the station (villagers stay in their village) and Milo wasn't allowed past the bridge, so nobody walked the line. Our pig lives in his own minecart in the yard ('loves it'). At midnight Milo turns ten and works it out like a kid who believes his grandpa: if she's on her way, the rail's broken.
twist: She was coming. On her way home from her sister's, 3,000 blocks out in a valley, a creeper had blown the line; the blast took the redstone torch of the last powered rail, which braked her cart to a stop at the edge of the crater. Mobs can't get out of a minecart on their own (the pig shows it), so Grandma has sat there for 22 years, facing home. Milo bridges the crater, lays rail, relights the gold rail and pushes; that evening her cart rolls into the buffer stop where Grandpa is waiting, and the station's activator rail sets her down beside him.

world.place: the rail town two valleys east of the carpeted village (Light Sleeper); its line runs south over a river bridge through the hills toward Grandma's sister's village
world.easter_egg: S01 and S13 (the station, looking south): the carpeted village of Light Sleeper on a far hill at frame right, under the sunset (west: the rail town lies east of it), carpet roofs in red and orange, the bell boxed in white wool. requests.direction: [A bubbly nine-year-old kid, fast, bright and energetic, telling a friend an amazing story; not whispery, breathy or soft]
[A bubbly nine-year-old kid, fast, bright and energetic, telling a friend an amazing story; not whispery, breathy or soft]
A rail station at sunset. Grandma: a woman in her seventies, warm and a little dry, a smile in her voice, full volume, unhurried; never breathy.

lines.text: My grandpa / has waited for / the SAME MINECART / for TWENTY-TWO / YEARS.
lines.direction: one quick breath, bright and amazed, a tiny lift on the number

lines.text: Every EVENING. / Empty RAIL. / He says, / "She's on her WAY."
lines.say: Every evening. Empty rail. <short pause> He says, "She's on her way."
lines.direction: matter-of-fact, then quoting him plainly and fondly, no impression of an old voice

lines.text: Mom says / Grandma LEFT him / for her SISTER'S.
lines.direction: the grin drops a notch, still full volume, repeating what grown-ups say
indignant on the last word, a kid taking Grandpa's side

lines.text: Our PIG / lives in / his OWN cart. / LOVES it.
lines.direction: proud and cheerful, sure of it

lines.text: Won't even / get out / for a CARROT.
lines.direction: laughing at how silly the pig is

lines.text: Grandpa won't leave / the STATION. / And I wasn't / allowed past / the BRIDGE.
lines.direction: explaining the rules fast, a little fed up with the second one

lines.text: At MIDNIGHT / I turned TEN. / If she's on her WAY, / the rail's BROKEN. / I packed RAILS.
lines.direction: lit up and brave, working it out as he goes, speeding up to the last phrase
big and a little out of breath, impressed with himself

lines.text: Then the rail / STOPPED. / A CREEPER hole, / grassed OVER.
lines.direction: a sudden stop in the voice on the second phrase, then puzzled, still full volume

lines.text: Past it, / a MINECART. / GRANDMA / in it. / Still facing HOME.
lines.direction: the speed goes out of him; wonder, not sadness; a beat before the last phrase, which lands warm

lines.text: I bridged / the HOLE, / laid RAILS, / PUSHED.
lines.say: I bridged the hole, <short pause> laid rails, <short pause> pushed.
lines.direction: fast and determined, a beat after each of the first two phrases, the last word like a launch

lines.text: That EVENING, / Grandpa was / waiting. / Like ALWAYS.
lines.direction: gentle and proud, smiling, full volume, slowing only on the last two words
warm and a little sheepish, a smile in it, as if she missed the bus

beats: S13: on 'waiting' the cart rolls off the bridge's north end (~45 blocks out) toward Grandpa, growing; the line ends with it ~15 blocks out (hop it there at the cut)

S14: the cart rolls in from the right over the powered activator rail at (0,1), knocks the buffer 0.3 s before L14, and the activator sets Grandma down standing on the rail bed at (0,1), facing Grandpa across the buffer stop; she says it; his head tips toward her on 'dear'
cut 0.6 s after the last word (payoff L14: the score drops out 0.45 s before, the hit on the buffer knock)
ending.loop: line 1 re-read: he really was waiting for the same minecart, and she really was on her way
